svg.text: ONE BLOCK: B AND C, JOINED AND SPLIT
Drawn at twice the face's size. SPLIT turns a stereo jack into L over R; JOIN back.
B · ONE BAND, IN AND OUT BELOW
Each half keeps its own SPLIT, as each frame does now: the input and the output split apart.
JOINED
a STEREO jack a side
THE INPUT SPLIT
L and R into the effect, one cord out
BOTH SPLIT
four jacks, four mono cords
C · AS A PEDAL, ONE SPLIT
One SPLIT for the block: the input and the output split together. The arrow says which way the sound goes.
JOINED
IN at the left edge, OUT at the right
SPLIT
L over R on both sides at once
C2 · AS A PEDAL, A SPLIT EACH SIDE
As C, but each side splits on its own, as now (B's behaviour in C's shape).
JOINED
THE INPUT SPLIT
BOTH SPLIT
THINGS TO WEIGH
· B: as wide as two halves (208); every control where it is now, only the header is shared
· C: 176 wide; one SPLIT means one switch flips four jacks: fewer keys, but the input and
the output of an effect can't be split apart (rarely wanted: an effect is stereo in, stereo out)
· C2: C's shape, B's freedom; two small SPLIT keys under the jacks
· split jacks stack L over R, as the face does now; the meter shows each jack's channel
